english: I can always tell when Josie's had a bit to drink... she loves to play footsie.
french: Je sais toujours quand Jo a un peu bu... Elle adore me faire du pied.
russian: По Джози всегда видно, когда она подвыпила... Её тянет флиртовать.
bulgarian: I can always tell when Josie's had a bit to drink... she loves to play footsie.

english: Nothing like a nightcap after a hard day! Can I get you anything, [Ari]?
french: Rien de tel qu'un dernier verre après une rude journée ! Je te sers quelque chose, [Ari] ?
russian: После долгого дня стаканчик холодненького — самое то. Тебе что-нибудь подать, [Ari]?
bulgarian: Nothing like a nightcap after a hard day! Can I get you anything, [Ari]?

english: I've been mixing drinks since I was kid, mom used to say I whipped up a mean hot chocolate.
french: Je fais des cocktails depuis que je suis petit. Maman disait toujours que j'étais imbattable pour préparer un super chocolat chaud en un rien de temps.
russian: Я мешаю напитки с детства — мама говорила, что у меня получался отличный горячий шоколад.
bulgarian: I've been mixing drinks since I was kid, mom used to say I whipped up a mean hot chocolate.

english: Hey there, [Ari].
french: Salut, [Ari] !
russian: Привет, [Ari].
bulgarian: Hey there, [Ari].

english: Josie insisted we stop by the Bathhouse, and I never could say no to her!
french: Jo a insisté pour qu'on s'arrête près des bains, et je ne peux jamais lui refuser quoi que ce soit !
russian: Джози настояла, чтобы мы заглянули в купальню, а я ей не умею отказывать!
bulgarian: Josie insisted we stop by the Bathhouse, and I never could say no to her!

english: Blustery out there, isn't it? Why don't you warm up with some soup from the pot!
french: Ça souffle, dehors, hein ? Réchauffe-toi donc avec un peu de soupe !
russian: На улице ветер, да? Загляни, согрейся супчиком из котла!
bulgarian: Blustery out there, isn't it? Why don't you warm up with some soup from the pot!

english: Hayden got me all the grain I needed! Time to get brewing!
french: Hayden m'a fourni toutes les céréales dont j'avais besoin ! C'est le moment de lancer la fermentation !
russian: Хейден достал мне всё зерно, что мне было нужно! Пора варить пиво!
bulgarian: Hayden got me all the grain I needed! Time to get brewing!

english: Luc got bugs in my lute again. Ah well... at least it's not termites this time around.
french: Luc a encore mis des insectes dans mon luth. Bon... au moins, ce ne sont pas des termites, cette fois-ci.
russian: Люк снова напустил жуков в мою лютню. Ну да ладно... хоть не термиты в этот раз.
bulgarian: Luc got bugs in my lute again. Ah well... at least it's not termites this time around.

english: The kids have so much energy! Kinda makes me want to play too.
french: Les enfants ont tellement d'énergie ! Ça me donne presque envie de jouer, moi aussi.
russian: У ребят столько энергии! Прямо самому поиграть захотелось.
bulgarian: The kids have so much energy! Kinda makes me want to play too.

english: I'd better check the stables, see if they need clearin' out.
french: Je ferais bien d'aller vérifier si les écuries ont besoin d'être nettoyées.
russian: Пойду проверю стойла, вдруг надо почистить.
bulgarian: I'd better check the stables, see if they need clearin' out.

english: The kids are usually fine on their own, but I like to check on them when they're in the Narrows.
french: Les enfants se débrouillent généralement bien tout seuls, mais j'aime garder un œil sur eux quand ils sont sur les Terrasses.
russian: Обычно детям и самим по себе окей, но когда они играют в Ущелье, мне спокойнее проведывать их время от времени.
bulgarian: The kids are usually fine on their own, but I like to check on them when they're in the Narrows.

english: A clean inn is a happy inn!
french: Une auberge propre est une auberge heureuse !
russian: Чистый трактир — счастливый трактир!
bulgarian: A clean inn is a happy inn!

english: The kids have been keeping their rooms clean lately!
french: Les enfants rangent leur chambre, depuis quelque temps !
russian: В последнее время дети свои комнаты сами убирают.
bulgarian: The kids have been keeping their rooms clean lately!

english: I came in here to tidy up, but there's not much to do if I'm being honest.
french: Je suis venu ici pour faire le ménage, mais pour être franc, il n'y a pas grand-chose à faire.
russian: Зашёл сюда прибраться, но, если честно, тут особо нечего делать.
bulgarian: I came in here to tidy up, but there's not much to do if I'm being honest.

english: Josie likes to keep the common area so clean it shines.
french: Jo aime que les parties communes soient rutilantes.
russian: Джози держит общую комнату такой чистой, аж блестит.
bulgarian: Josie likes to keep the common area so clean it shines.

english: Folks being me.
french: Les gens en question, c'est moi.
russian: Многим — это мне, например.
bulgarian: Folks being me.

english: Juniper didn't take too kindly to my idea of bringing drinks into the bath. I'm just saying, I think folks would like it.
french: Juniper n'a guère apprécié mon idée d'apporter à boire dans le bain. Je me dis que les gens aimeraient ça, voilà tout.
russian: Джунипер не оценила мою идею приносить напитки в купальню. А я вот думаю, многим бы понравилось.
bulgarian: Juniper didn't take too kindly to my idea of bringing drinks into the bath. I'm just saying, I think folks would like it.

english: When I was with the band, we got up a heck of a lot earlier than this. Up and at'em!
french: Quand j'étais avec mon groupe, on se levait bien plus tôt que ça. Allez hop, debout !
russian: Когда я был в группе, мы вставали куда раньше. Подъём — и вперёд!
bulgarian: When I was with the band, we got up a heck of a lot earlier than this. Up and at'em!

english: Fall's a good season for the Inn. Everyone wants to get cozy by the hearth and enjoy each other's company.
french: L'automne est une bonne saison pour l'auberge. Tout le monde a envie de s'installer confortablement près du feu et de profiter de la compagnie.
russian: Осень — отличное время для трактира. Все хотят уюта у очага и душевной компании.
bulgarian: Fall's a good season for the Inn. Everyone wants to get cozy by the hearth and enjoy each other's company.

english: Today's our busiest evening of the week. Whole town's going to be here, soon enough.
french: Ce soir, c'est la soirée la plus chargée de la semaine. Toute la ville va bientôt arriver.
russian: Сегодня самый загруженный вечер недели. Скоро тут будет весь город.
bulgarian: Today's our busiest evening of the week. Whole town's going to be here, soon enough.

english: The soup smells great today! Have yourself a bowl, it's always on the house!
french: La soupe sent drôlement bon, aujourd'hui ! Sers-t'en un bol, c'est toujours la maison qui régale !
russian: Сегодня суп особенно ароматный! Угощайся, он у нас всегда за счёт заведения!
bulgarian: The soup smells great today! Have yourself a bowl, it's always on the house!

english: Now life's fun AND good. Real good.
french: Maintenant, la vie est marrante ET agréable. Vraiment agréable.
russian: Теперь жизнь и весёлая и хорошая. Очень хорошая.
bulgarian: Now life's fun AND good. Real good.

english: Life with the band was fun, but a family and a hearth?
french: La vie avec le groupe, c'était marrant, mais une famille et un foyer ?
russian: Жизнь в группе была весёлой, но семья и очаг?..
bulgarian: Life with the band was fun, but a family and a hearth?

english: Let me know if we can get you something from the kitchen, [Ari].
french: Dis-moi si tu as besoin qu'on t'apporte quelque chose de la cuisine, [Ari].
russian: Дай знать, если захочешь чего-нибудь с кухни, [Ari].
bulgarian: Let me know if we can get you something from the kitchen, [Ari].

english: Mistria's been good to me.
french: Mistria m'a bien accueilli.
russian: Мистрия хорошо ко мне отнеслась.
bulgarian: Mistria's been good to me.

english: Good to meet you, [Ari], I'm Hemlock. If you ever need a hot meal or a cold drink, be sure to stop by the $Sleeping Dragon Inn$.
french: Ravi de faire ta connaissance, [Ari], je suis Hemlock. Si tu as besoin d'un bon repas ou d'un rafraîchissement, passe nous voir à l'$auberge du Dragon qui dort$.
russian: Рад знакомству, [Ari], я Хемлок. Если вдруг захочешь съесть горяченького или выпить холодненького — заглядывай в $трактир «Спящий дракон»$.
bulgarian: Good to meet you, [Ari], I'm Hemlock. If you ever need a hot meal or a cold drink, be sure to stop by the $Sleeping Dragon Inn$.

english: There's always a cauldron of hearty soup kept hot for anyone who wants a bowl!
french: Il y a toujours sur le feu une bonne marmite de soupe pour réchauffer ceux qui en voudraient un bol !
russian: У нас всегда стоит котёл с наваристым супом — для всех, кто захочет!
bulgarian: There's always a cauldron of hearty soup kept hot for anyone who wants a bowl!

english: Now who do we have here? Are you the new farmer everyone's been talking about?
french: Tiens, qui voilà ? Tu es <she>la nouvelle fermière dont tout le monde parle ?</she><he>le nouveau fermier dont tout le monde parle ?</he><they>la personne venue reprendre la ferme et dont tout le monde parle</they> ?
russian:
А кто это у нас тут? Ты

те самые новые фермер

та самая новая фермеркатот самый новый фермерто самое новое фермер, о ком все говорят?
bulgarian: Now who do we have here? Are you the new farmer everyone's been talking about?

english: Gets pretty quiet when he drinks alone though.
french: Mais il est assez taciturne quand il prend un verre tout seul.
russian: Хотя когда пьёт в одиночку, становится совсем неразговорчивым.
bulgarian: Gets pretty quiet when he drinks alone though.

english: Wonder what's on his mind?
french: Je me demande à quoi il pense.
russian: Интересно, что у него на уме?
bulgarian: Wonder what's on his mind?

english: Hayden's a good guy.
french: Hayden est un brave homme.
russian: Хейден хороший малый.
bulgarian: Hayden's a good guy.

english: I heard Hayden's prize chicken got out again. Henrietta's a right rascal.
french: Il paraît que la poule de concours d'Hayden s'est encore enfuie. Henrietta est une vraie friponne.
russian: Слышал, курица Хейдена опять сбежала. Генриетта та ещё шельма.
bulgarian: I heard Hayden's prize chicken got out again. Henrietta's a right rascal.

english: Josie's partial to herbal teas in the afternoon. Eiland recommended this one. He's got good taste.
french: Jo a un faible pour les thés à base de plantes, l'après-midi. Eiland lui a conseillé celui-ci. Il a bon goût.
russian: Джози любит травяной чай днём. Этот посоветовал Эйланд. У него вкус отменный.
bulgarian: Josie's partial to herbal teas in the afternoon. Eiland recommended this one. He's got good taste.

english: Holt's been whittling a rhinoceros beetle for Luc. He's going to go crazy for it!
french: Holt a sculpté un scarabée rhinocéros pour Luc. Il va être fou de joie !
russian: Хольт вырезает Люку жука-носорога. Тот точно с ума сойдёт от радости!
bulgarian: Holt's been whittling a rhinoceros beetle for Luc. He's going to go crazy for it!

english: Josie says he's been like this since they were kids!
french: Jo dit qu'il est comme ça depuis qu'ils sont gamins !
russian: Джози говорит, он с детства такой!
bulgarian: Josie says he's been like this since they were kids!

english: Holt's puns are so painful, they go all the way around to being funny again.
french: Les blagues de Holt sont si mauvaises que ça en devient vraiment drôle, pour finir.
russian: Шутки Холта такие ужасные, аж смешно становится.
bulgarian: Holt's puns are so painful, they go all the way around to being funny again.

english: You're really making a home for yourself here! It takes a bit of pluck, don't it?
french: Tu cherches vraiment à faire ton trou ici, hein ! Ça demande un certain courage, quand même.
russian: Ты и правда неплохо здесь обживаешься! Для этого нужна смелость, да?
bulgarian: You're really making a home for yourself here! It takes a bit of pluck, don't it?

english: Morning, [Ari]! We've got a hot cup of tea on the menu... you'll wake right up!
french: Bonjour, [Ari] ! On a une tasse de thé chaud à la carte... Ça va te réveiller tout de suite !
russian: Доброе утро, [Ari]! У нас в меню горячий чай... сразу проснёшься!
bulgarian: Morning, [Ari]! We've got a hot cup of tea on the menu... you'll wake right up!

english: [Ari], how are ya? Don't work too hard now.
french: [Ari], comment ça va ? Ne travaille pas trop dur.
russian: Как ты, [Ari]? Не переусердствуй там.
bulgarian: [Ari], how are ya? Don't work too hard now.

english: Sleeping Dragon Inn's here to serve. How can I help you?
french: L'auberge du Dragon qui dort est à ton service. En quoi puis-je t'aider ?
russian: Трактир «Спящий дракон» к твоим услугам. Чем могу помочь?
bulgarian: Sleeping Dragon Inn's here to serve. How can I help you?

english: I'll leave singing on the job to Josie!
french: Pour ce qui est de chanter en travaillant, je laisse ça à Jo !
russian: Пусть пение на работе остаётся за Джози!
bulgarian: I'll leave singing on the job to Josie!

english: I don't usually hum while I work. I get carried away and end up picking up my lute!
french: En général, je ne fredonne pas pendant le travail. Sinon je me laisse emporter, et je finis par prendre mon luth !
russian: Обычно я не напеваю за работой. А то увлекаюсь и хватаю лютню!
bulgarian: I don't usually hum while I work. I get carried away and end up picking up my lute!

english: Morning, [Ari]! I'm just finishing up breakfast, but let me know if you need anything.
french: Bonjour, [Ari] ! Je suis en train de terminer le petit-déjeuner, mais dis-moi si tu as besoin de quelque chose.
russian: Доброе утро, [Ari]! Я как раз доедаю завтрак, но если что нужно — скажи.
bulgarian: Morning, [Ari]! I'm just finishing up breakfast, but let me know if you need anything.

english: You coming to the Inn tonight? The company will be good and the drinks even better!
french: Tu viens à l'auberge, ce soir ? Il y aura de la bonne compagnie et des boissons encore meilleures !
russian: Сегодня придёшь в трактир? Компания будет отличной, а выпивка — ещё лучше!
bulgarian: You coming to the Inn tonight? The company will be good and the drinks even better!

english: Josie's a beauty with a generous heart, but her voice was what first got me. I was like a moth to the flame.
french: Jo est une vraie beauté et a le cœur sur la main, mais c'est sa voix qui m'a d'abord séduit. J'étais attiré comme un papillon par la lumière.
russian: Джози — красавица с добрым сердцем, но сначала меня покорил её голос. Как мотылёк на огонь.
bulgarian: Josie's a beauty with a generous heart, but her voice was what first got me. I was like a moth to the flame.

english: My lute could use tuning, but I'll leave it for tomorrow. Sleep's callin'.
french: Mon luth aurait bien besoin d'être accordé, mais je ferai ça demain. Le sommeil m'appelle.
russian: Лютню бы поднастроить, но это завтра. Сейчас — сон зовёт.
bulgarian: My lute could use tuning, but I'll leave it for tomorrow. Sleep's callin'.

english: Hey [Ari], make yourself comfortable! I gotta get the tea going, I like to have it ready for Jo when she comes back.
french: Salut, [Ari], mets-toi à l'aise ! J'ai lancé la préparation du thé, j'aime bien qu'il soit prêt pour Jo quand elle rentre.
russian: Привет, [Ari], устраивайся поудобнее! Я только за чаем: люблю, чтобы к приходу Джо он был готов.
bulgarian: Hey [Ari], make yourself comfortable! I gotta get the tea going, I like to have it ready for Jo when she comes back.

english: Good on you. I knew you'd crack that shell sooner or later!
french: Tant mieux. Je savais que tu finirais par percer sa carapace.
russian: Рад за тебя. Я знал, что рано или поздно ты пробьёшь его толстую шкуру!
bulgarian: Good on you. I knew you'd crack that shell sooner or later!

english: March has really taken a shine to you, hasn't he?
french: March commence à t'apprécier, n'est-ce pas ?
russian:
Я смотрю, ты

приглянулись

приглянуласьприглянулсяприглянулось Марту.
bulgarian: March has really taken a shine to you, hasn't he?

english: Market's tomorrow... maybe I'll stop in and find a little gift for Josie.
french: Il y a le marché, demain... Je vais peut-être m'y arrêter pour y trouver un petit cadeau pour Jo.
russian: Завтра базар... Может, загляну и выберу Джози какой-нибудь подарок.
bulgarian: Market's tomorrow... maybe I'll stop in and find a little gift for Josie.

english: You won't find a hotter meal or a fluffier bed than at the Sleeping Dragon Inn!
french: Jamais tu ne trouveras un repas plus chaud et un lit plus moelleux qu'à l'auberge du Dragon qui dort !
russian: Блюд горячее и постели мягче, чем в «Спящем драконе», не найти!
bulgarian: You won't find a hotter meal or a fluffier bed than at the Sleeping Dragon Inn!

english: Morning, [Ari]! Some breakfast for you? We've got fresh butter in from Hayden's farm!
french: Bonjour, [Ari] ! Tu veux un petit-déjeuner ? On a du beurre tout frais de la ferme d'Hayden !
russian: Доброе утро, [Ari]! Завтракать будешь? У нас свежее масло с фермы Хейдена!
bulgarian: Morning, [Ari]! Some breakfast for you? We've got fresh butter in from Hayden's farm!

english: Anyone need anything, you just say the word! That includes you, [Ari]!
french: Si quelqu'un a besoin de quoi que ce soit, il suffit de le dire ! Ça vaut pour toi aussi, [Ari] !
russian: Если кому-то что-то нужно, просто скажите! Это и тебя касается, [Ari]!
bulgarian: Anyone need anything, you just say the word! That includes you, [Ari]!

english: Just getting things in order around here. Let me know if I can get you something.
french: Je suis seulement en train de mettre un peu d'ordre. Dis-moi si je peux te servir quelque chose.
russian: Навожу тут порядок. Если что надо — не стесняйся.
bulgarian: Just getting things in order around here. Let me know if I can get you something.

english: Morning! Wish the audience was more attentive, but you can't beat the venue!
french: Bonjour ! J'aimerais que le public soit plus attentif, mais le lieu est imbattable !
russian: Доброе утро! Жаль, публика не очень внимательная, но площадка-то отличная!
bulgarian: Morning! Wish the audience was more attentive, but you can't beat the venue!

english: Hope you're enjoying the performance, [Ari]!
french: J'espère que le spectacle te plaît, [Ari] !
russian: Надеюсь, тебе нравится выступление, [Ari]!
bulgarian: Hope you're enjoying the performance, [Ari]!

english: Hey [Ari]! You're lookin' like you could use a good meal. Why don't you put your feet up?
french: Salut, [Ari] ! Un bon repas ne te ferait pas de mal, j'ai l'impression. Pourquoi ne pas t'installer ?
russian: Привет, [Ari]! Выглядишь так, будто тебе пора подкрепиться. Присаживайся!
bulgarian: Hey [Ari]! You're lookin' like you could use a good meal. Why don't you put your feet up?

english: We've got to get the place ready for the folks who come by in the evening!
french: On doit tout mettre en place pour celles et ceux qui viendront ce soir !
russian: Надо подготовиться к вечернему наплыву гостей!
bulgarian: We've got to get the place ready for the folks who come by in the evening!

english: Rain tends to bring people together, which is why a rainy morning is all hands on deck at the Sleeping Dragon Inn.
french: La pluie a tendance à rapprocher les gens, c'est pour ça que durant les matinées pluvieuses, tout le monde est sur le pont, à l'auberge du Dragon qui dort.
russian: Дождь сближает людей, потому в такие утра в «Спящем драконе» работы всем хватает.
bulgarian: Rain tends to bring people together, which is why a rainy morning is all hands on deck at the Sleeping Dragon Inn.

english: Nothing like mulled cider on a rainy day, [Ari]!
french: Rien de tel qu'un cidre chaud quand il pleut, [Ari] !
russian: Ничто так не греет в дождливый день, как глинтвейн, [Ari]!
bulgarian: Nothing like mulled cider on a rainy day, [Ari]!

english: Rainy days are perfect for some hot soup. Feel free to help yourself! The pot's open to all.
french: Les jours de pluie sont parfaits pour manger une soupe chaude. N'hésite pas à te servir ! La marmite est là pour tout le monde.
russian: В такую погоду тарелка горячего супа — самое то. Угощайся, котёл для всех!
bulgarian: Rainy days are perfect for some hot soup. Feel free to help yourself! The pot's open to all.

english: We were a little low on ingredients at the Inn, so I popped on over to pick some things up.
french: On était un peu à court d'ingrédients, à l'auberge, alors j'ai fait un saut ici pour prendre une ou deux choses.
russian: В трактире немного не хватало ингредиентов, вот я и сбегал за продуктами.
bulgarian: We were a little low on ingredients at the Inn, so I popped on over to pick some things up.

english: Reina chopped all the ingredients last night... she's always one step ahead of me!
french: Reina a taillé tous les ingrédients, hier soir... Elle a toujours un temps d'avance sur moi !
russian: Рейна всё нарезала ещё вчера... она всегда на шаг впереди!
bulgarian: Reina chopped all the ingredients last night... she's always one step ahead of me!

english: Reina ought to be back soon, if you were looking for her.
french: Reina ne devrait pas tarder à revenir, si c'est elle que tu cherches.
russian: Рейна скоро вернётся, если ты её ищешь.
bulgarian: Reina ought to be back soon, if you were looking for her.

english: Reina really outdid herself on today's soup. Take a gander, grab a bowl!
french: Reina s'est vraiment surpassée avec la soupe du jour. Jette un coup d'œil et attrape un bol !
russian: Рейна сегодня такой суп сварила — пальчики оближешь. Загляни, попробуй!
bulgarian: Reina really outdid herself on today's soup. Take a gander, grab a bowl!

english: Normally we'd be having a Saturday Market in the town square right now, but it's been anything but normal since the earthquake.
french: En temps normal, le marché du samedi devrait être installé sur la place principale, mais il n'y a plus grand-chose de normal depuis le tremblement de terre.
russian: Сейчас бы на площади у нас проходил Субботний базар, но после землетрясения всё не как обычно.
bulgarian: Normally we'd be having a Saturday Market in the town square right now, but it's been anything but normal since the earthquake.

english: When I told her we didn't have anything that special, she insisted I check again... and we did!
french: Quand je lui ai dit qu'on n'avait rien de tel ici, elle a insisté pour que je revérifie... et on en a trouvé !
russian: Когда я сказал ей, что у нас не найдётся таких редкостей, она потребовала, чтобы я проверил ещё раз... И они нашлись!
bulgarian: When I told her we didn't have anything that special, she insisted I check again... and we did!

english: Seridia always insists on the finest dishes and silverware when she eats here.
french: Seridia insiste pour que je sorte la belle vaisselle et l'argenterie quand elle mange ici.
russian: Когда Серидия заходит к нам поесть, она требует, чтобы мы доставали из шкафов лучшее столовое серебро!
bulgarian: Seridia always insists on the finest dishes and silverware when she eats here.

english: Settling in alright, [Ari]? I was new to Mistria once, too. Don't be shy if you need someone to show you the ropes.
french: Tu t'installes bien, [Ari] ? Moi aussi j'ai un jour été nouveau à Mistria. N'hésite pas à me demander si tu as besoin qu'on te montre comment ça fonctionne.
russian: Осваиваешься, [Ari]? Я ведь тоже когда-то был новеньким в Мистрии. Обращайся, если что, — помогу!
bulgarian: Settling in alright, [Ari]? I was new to Mistria once, too. Don't be shy if you need someone to show you the ropes.

english: Sleeping Dragon Inn, at your service! Kick your feet up and stay awhile.
french: L'auberge du Dragon qui dort, à ton service ! Installe-toi confortablement et reste un moment.
russian: «Спящий дракон» к твоим услугам! Присаживайся, отдыхай.
bulgarian: Sleeping Dragon Inn, at your service! Kick your feet up and stay awhile.

english: It all started when we won a bet with March and Olric's old man...
french: Tout a commencé quand on a gagné un pari contre le père de March et Olric...
russian: Всё началось с того, как мы выиграли пари у отца Марта и Олрика...
bulgarian: It all started when we won a bet with March and Olric's old man...

english: Did I ever tell you the story of how we got this stove?
french: Je t'ai déjà raconté comment on avait obtenu ce poêle ?
russian: Я тебе когда-нибудь рассказывал, откуда у нас эта плита?
bulgarian: Did I ever tell you the story of how we got this stove?

english: Menu's looking good today! Grab a seat and thaw yourself out!
french: La carte du jour est appétissante ! Attrape un siège et réchauffe-toi !
russian: Сегодня в меню много вкусного! Присаживайся, согревайся!
bulgarian: Menu's looking good today! Grab a seat and thaw yourself out!

english: Hey, [Ari]. I'm just tidying up- let me know if you need something.
french: Salut, [Ari] ! Je suis en train de faire le ménage, dis-moi s'il te faut quoi que ce soit.
russian: Привет, [Ari]. Я тут прибираюсь — скажи, если что-то нужно.
bulgarian: Hey, [Ari]. I'm just tidying up- let me know if you need something.

english: It's about time for dinner, I think. There's always room at our table, [Ari]!
french: C'est presque l'heure du dîner, je crois. Il y a toujours une place à notre table, [Ari] !
russian: Похоже, пора ужинать. За нашим столом всегда найдётся место, [Ari]!
bulgarian: It's about time for dinner, I think. There's always room at our table, [Ari]!

english: Can't talk now, [Ari]! Promised I'd take over for Josie at the register.
french: Je ne peux pas discuter maintenant, [Ari] ! J'ai promis à Jo de la remplacer à la caisse.
russian: Сейчас не могу болтать, [Ari]! Обещал подменить Джози у стойки.
bulgarian: Can't talk now, [Ari]! Promised I'd take over for Josie at the register.

english: It doesn't take too much effort to talk Josie into a duet, hah. Stick around a while and we'll serenade you!
french: Ça ne demande pas un gros effort de convaincre Jo de faire un duo. Reste un moment et on te chantera la sérénade !
russian: Уговорить Джози на дуэт не так уж и сложно, ха. Оставайся подольше — споём для тебя!
bulgarian: It doesn't take too much effort to talk Josie into a duet, hah. Stick around a while and we'll serenade you!

english: Sometimes a show just didn't cover room and board.
french: Parfois, ce qu'on gagnait pour un spectacle ne couvrait même pas le gîte et le couvert.
russian: Иногда гонорара за концерт не хватало даже на постой и еду.
bulgarian: Sometimes a show just didn't cover room and board.

english: I washed so many dishes while I was touring with the band.
french: J'ai lavé tellement d'assiettes à l'époque où je tournais avec le groupe.
russian: Когда я гастролировал с группой, перемыл столько посуды...
bulgarian: I washed so many dishes while I was touring with the band.

english: These kids sure do a great job of keeping Mistria safe... from getting too boring.
french: Ce qui est sûr, c'est que ces enfants protègent Mistria... de l'ennui.
russian: Детки отлично справляются со своим долгом защищать Мистрию... от скуки.
bulgarian: These kids sure do a great job of keeping Mistria safe... from getting too boring.

english: Our selection is more limited than it used to be...
french: Nous avons moins de choix qu'à une époque...
russian: Выбор у нас теперь поскромнее, чем раньше...
bulgarian: Our selection is more limited than it used to be...

english: But scarcity breeds ingenuity!
french: Mais la pénurie rend ingénieux !
russian: Зато нужда — мать изобретательности!
bulgarian: But scarcity breeds ingenuity!

english: Stop by for a drink some evening, won't you?
french: Pourquoi ne pas t'arrêter prendre un verre, un de ces soirs ?
russian: Заглядывай как-нибудь вечерком пропустить стаканчик, а?
bulgarian: Stop by for a drink some evening, won't you?

english: I know it could do with some repairs and a fresh coat of paint or two...
french: N'oublie pas que si tu cherches à bien manger, en bonne compagnie, l'auberge du Dragon qui dort est là pour ça !
russian: Понимаю, что его кое-где пора подлатать или подкрасить...
bulgarian: I know it could do with some repairs and a fresh coat of paint or two...

english: But I think you'll find it's a nice place to live!
russian: Но я думаю, ты скоро увидишь, что живётся тут хорошо!
bulgarian: But I think you'll find it's a nice place to live!

english: How do you like town so far, [Ari]?
french: La ville te plaît, pour l'instant, [Ari] ? Elle est jolie, hein ?
russian: Ну как тебе наш городок, [Ari]?
bulgarian: How do you like town so far, [Ari]?

english: Reina gets everyone eventually!
french: Reina finit toujours par convaincre les gens !
russian: Рейна до всех добирается!
bulgarian: Reina gets everyone eventually!

english: Now that you've moved in, it's only a matter of time before my oldest will have you taste testing her dishes.
french: Maintenant que tu as emménagé à Mistria, il ne faudra pas longtemps pour que ma fille aînée te fasse goûter ses plats.
russian: Раз ты тут живёшь, скоро начнёшь дегустировать блюда моей старшей дочки. Это лишь вопрос времени.
bulgarian: Now that you've moved in, it's only a matter of time before my oldest will have you taste testing her dishes.

english: Welcome to the Sleeping Dragon Inn. Kick your feet up a while!
french: Bienvenue à l'auberge du Dragon qui dort ! Repose-toi un moment.
russian: Добро пожаловать в «Спящий дракон»! Присаживайся, отдохни.
bulgarian: Welcome to the Sleeping Dragon Inn. Kick your feet up a while!

english: Welcome to the Sleeping Dragon Inn! Forget about the rain and warm up with food and friends.
french: Bienvenue à l'auberge du Dragon qui dort ! Oublie la pluie et viens te réchauffer avec de bons plats et des amis.
russian: Добро пожаловать в «Спящий дракон»! Забудь про дождь — согрейся едой и дружеским теплом.
bulgarian: Welcome to the Sleeping Dragon Inn! Forget about the rain and warm up with food and friends.

english: Might be biased, though.
french: Mais je ne suis peut-être pas objectif.
russian: Хотя я, может, и не совсем объективен.
bulgarian: Might be biased, though.

english: Welcome to the Sleeping Dragon Inn! Best inn in Mistria.
french: Bienvenue à l'auberge du Dragon qui dort ! La meilleure auberge de tout Mistria !
russian: Добро пожаловать в «Спящий дракон»! Лучший трактир в Мистрии.
bulgarian: Welcome to the Sleeping Dragon Inn! Best inn in Mistria.

english: The Inn's a little cozier in winter, isn't it? Funny how that works.
french: L'auberge est un peu plus cosy en hiver, hein ? C'est marrant, à quoi ça tient.
russian: Зимой тут как-то уютнее, да? Странно, но факт.
bulgarian: The Inn's a little cozier in winter, isn't it? Funny how that works.

english: Whew! Worked up an appetite trying to keep up with the kids.
french: Pfiou ! Ça m'a creusé l'appétit d'essayer de suivre les enfants.
russian: Уф! Пока с детьми носился, аппетит нагулял.
bulgarian: Whew! Worked up an appetite trying to keep up with the kids.

english: Take a load off! The drinks are cold and the cooking is unbelievable!
french: Installe-toi et détends-toi ! Les boissons sont fraîches et la cuisine, imbattable !
russian: Отдохни! Напитки холодные, а еда — просто пальчики оближешь!
bulgarian: Take a load off! The drinks are cold and the cooking is unbelievable!

english: You get it, right? How special it is to come to Mistria from afar and make it your home.
french: Tu comprends, hein ? Ce que ça représente d'arriver de loin et de faire de Mistria son chez-soi.
russian: Ты ведь понимаешь, да? Как это здорово: приехать в Мистрию издалека и назвать её своим домом.
bulgarian: You get it, right? How special it is to come to Mistria from afar and make it your home.

english: You hungry? Let me know if we can whip something up for you!
french: Tu as faim ? Dis-moi si tu veux qu'on te prépare un petit quelque chose vite fait !
russian: Есть хочешь? Скажи — чего-нибудь вкусненького приготовим!
bulgarian: You hungry? Let me know if we can whip something up for you!

english: All that running around must have worked up a thirst. Let me know if I can get you anything!
french: Courir partout comme ça a dû te donner soif. Dis-moi si je peux te servir quelque chose.
russian: После такой беготни вокруг, наверное, пить хочется. Скажи, принести чего?
bulgarian: All that running around must have worked up a thirst. Let me know if I can get you anything!

english: Thanks, [Ari]!
french: Merci, [Ari] !
russian: Спасибо, [Ari]!
bulgarian: Thanks, [Ari]!

english: Oh, you got me something for my birthday? I can't wait to show Josie!
french: Oh, c'est pour mon anniversaire ? J'ai hâte de montrer ça à Jo !
russian: О, это мне на день рождения? Надо Джози показать!
bulgarian: Oh, you got me something for my birthday? I can't wait to show Josie!

english: You got me =Etouffee=? Josie and I love this, it's one of our favorites! Can't wait to share it with her. Thanks, [Ari].
french: Tu m'offres un =gumbo= ? Jo et moi, on adore ça. C'est un de nos plats préférés ! J'ai hâte de le déguster avec elle. Merci, [Ari].
russian:
Ты

принесли

принеслапринёспринесло =этуфе=? Мы с Джози его обожаем! Не терпится с ней поделиться. Спасибо, [Ari]!
bulgarian: You got me =Etouffee=? Josie and I love this, it's one of our favorites! Can't wait to share it with her. Thanks, [Ari].

english: You sure this is for me? Well, if you say so...
french: C'est pour moi, vraiment ? Bien, si tu le dis...
russian: Это точно мне? Ну, раз так...
bulgarian: You sure this is for me? Well, if you say so...

english: This is for me? I gotta show Josie!
french: C'est pour moi ? Quand je vais montrer ça à Jo !
russian: Это мне? Надо Джози показать!
bulgarian: This is for me? I gotta show Josie!

english: Looks delicious! Thanks, [Ari].
french: Je sens que je vais me régaler ! Merci, [Ari].
russian: Выглядит очень вкусно! Спасибо, [Ari].
bulgarian: Looks delicious! Thanks, [Ari].

english: This is mighty thoughtful of you, [Ari]. Thanks, I'm going to enjoy it.
french: C'est vraiment très gentil de ta part, [Ari]. Merci, je vais me régaler.
russian: Это очень обдуманно, [Ari]. Спасибо, я наслажусь этим подарком.
bulgarian: This is mighty thoughtful of you, [Ari]. Thanks, I'm going to enjoy it.

english: Would you look at that! I was just daydreaming about this. Thanks, [Ari]!
french: Ça alors ! J'en rêvais justement. Merci, [Ari] !
russian: Вот это да! Я как раз мечтал об этом. Спасибо, [Ari]!
bulgarian: Would you look at that! I was just daydreaming about this. Thanks, [Ari]!

english: You know me so well! I'll make time to properly toast you with Josie later.
french: Tu me connais si bien ! Je lèverai mon verre à ta santé avec Jo tout à l'heure.
russian: Ты меня знаешь как облупленного! Позже с Джози тебя как следует поблагодарим.
bulgarian: You know me so well! I'll make time to properly toast you with Josie later.

english: Hot dang, that smells amazing! This is something worth changing your dinner plans for, eh?
french: Qu'est-ce que ça sent bon ! Ce n'est pas ce qui était prévu pour le dîner, mais j'aime autant !
russian: Ух ты, какой аромат! Ради такого можно и планы на ужин поменять, правда?
bulgarian: Hot dang, that smells amazing! This is something worth changing your dinner plans for, eh?

english: Hey, thanks.
french: Oh, merci.
russian: Эй, спасибо.
bulgarian: Hey, thanks.

english: Come on now, not even Dell hands out newts as gifts.
french: Sérieusement ? Même Dell ne m'a jamais offert de triton.
russian: Да ладно тебе, даже Делл не дарит тритонов!
bulgarian: Come on now, not even Dell hands out newts as gifts.

english: I like =Coffee= well enough, but I wonder if Darcy's got a dark =Beer= back there...
french: J'aime bien le =café=, mais je me demande si Darcy n'aurait pas plutôt de la =bière= brune en réserve...
russian: К =кофе= я отношусь нормально, но интересно, есть ли у Дарси тёмное =пиво=?
bulgarian: I like =Coffee= well enough, but I wonder if Darcy's got a dark =Beer= back there...

english: Josie loves tea, but I somehow never got a taste for it. =Coffee=, however... I do like a bit in the evening, from time to time.
french: Jo adore le thé, mais ce n'est pas mon truc. En revanche, je me prends parfois un petit =café= le soir.
russian: Джози обожает чай, а я так к нему и не прикипел. А вот =кофе=... иногда вечерами люблю выпить немного.
bulgarian: Josie loves tea, but I somehow never got a taste for it. =Coffee=, however... I do like a bit in the evening, from time to time.

english: I think I'm a medium roast guy... I'm medium about most things.
french: J'ai une préférence pour un café au goût équilibré... D'ailleurs, je cherche l'équilibre dans à peu près tout.
russian: Кажется, я больше люблю среднюю обжарку... Да и в целом я люблю всё умеренное.
bulgarian: I think I'm a medium roast guy... I'm medium about most things.

english: Milk, no milk... I like =Coffee= either way.
french: Avec ou sans lait, peu importe. Tant que j'ai mon =café= !
russian: С молоком, без молока... =Кофе= мне нравится и так и так.
bulgarian: Milk, no milk... I like =Coffee= either way.

english: Jo's a knockout, and Louis' outfits are the sucker punch!
french: Jo est une vraie beauté, et les vêtements de Louis savent la mettre en valeur !
russian: Джо — сногсшибательная, а наряды от Луи — прямо в сердце!
bulgarian: Jo's a knockout, and Louis' outfits are the sucker punch!

english: Louis could sell me a vest, sight unseen. They're always a hit with me.
french: Louis pourrait me vendre ce qu'il veut. À chaque fois, ses vêtements me vont à la perfection.
russian: Луи может продать мне жилет вслепую. Мне всё его по вкусу.
bulgarian: Louis could sell me a vest, sight unseen. They're always a hit with me.

english: Louis really gets the difference between trend and style.
french: Louis sait la distinction entre mode et style.
russian: Луи отлично понимает разницу между модой и стилем.
bulgarian: Louis really gets the difference between trend and style.

english: You ever shop for clothes with Reina? Might be fun for the two of you.
french: Tu as déjà fait du shopping chez Louis avec Reina ? Vous passeriez un bon moment ensemble.
russian:
Ты когда-нибудь

ходили

ходилаходилходило за одеждой с Рейной? Вам бы понравилось вдвоём.
bulgarian: You ever shop for clothes with Reina? Might be fun for the two of you.

english: I'd rather stand than sit, so I didn't really get why Jo was so crazy about the armchairs we got from Merri... but my baby is right. That's a comfortable chair.
french: Je suis plutôt du genre à rester debout. Je n'avais pas compris pourquoi Jo adorait ces fauteuils achetés chez Merri... mais elle avait raison. On est bien dedans.
russian: Я больше стоять люблю, так что не понимал, чего Джо в таком восторге от кресел Мэрри... но детка права. Какие же они удобные.
bulgarian: I'd rather stand than sit, so I didn't really get why Jo was so crazy about the armchairs we got from Merri... but my baby is right. That's a comfortable chair.

english: Merri says she's got an ottoman that looks like a beetle... I've gotta show Luc.
french: Merri dit qu'elle a un pouf en forme de scarabée... Il faut que je montre ça à Luc.
russian: Мэрри говорит, у неё есть пуф в форме жука... надо показать Люку.
bulgarian: Merri says she's got an ottoman that looks like a beetle... I've gotta show Luc.

english: Jo asked me to set a furniture allowance after she went on a buying spree at Merri's a while back... I don't really have the heart to enforce it, though.
french: Jo m'avait demandé de fixer un plafond de dépenses après avoir fait des folies chez Merri une fois... En fait, j'ai du mal à le lui rappeler.
russian: Однажды Джо запойно закупилась у Мэрри и тогда попросила меня ввести мебельный лимит... но мне трудно настаивать.
bulgarian: Jo asked me to set a furniture allowance after she went on a buying spree at Merri's a while back... I don't really have the heart to enforce it, though.

english: Maple wants furniture that screams princess... I'm keeping my eyes peeled.
french: Maple aimerait des meubles de princesse pour sa chambre... Je garde l'œil ouvert.
russian: Мэйпл хочет какую-нибудь кричащую мебель, как у принцесс... Вот, ищу подходящее.
bulgarian: Maple wants furniture that screams princess... I'm keeping my eyes peeled.

english: Can you help me make heads or tails of this money fortune? "All that glitters is not gold, unless the glitter leaps from gold." Stillwell should come with a manual, if I'm being honest.
bulgarian: Can you help me make heads or tails of this money fortune? "All that glitters is not gold, unless the glitter leaps from gold." Stillwell should come with a manual, if I'm being honest.

english: I'll leave the love fortunes for Reina... what better fortune could I have than marrying my sweetheart Josie?
bulgarian: I'll leave the love fortunes for Reina... what better fortune could I have than marrying my sweetheart Josie?

english: I try to tell Luc not to ask for fortunes for all his little bug friends... it upsets Stillwell. He must be a bug fan, too.
bulgarian: I try to tell Luc not to ask for fortunes for all his little bug friends... it upsets Stillwell. He must be a bug fan, too.

english: In Stillwell's words, "the creaking of the wheel is the voice of reason". In my words, "I want my money back."
bulgarian: In Stillwell's words, "the creaking of the wheel is the voice of reason". In my words, "I want my money back."

english: I should ask him what kind of pomade he uses...
french: Je devrais lui demander quelle sorte de gel il utilise...
russian: Надо будет спросить, какой помадой он пользуется...
bulgarian: I should ask him what kind of pomade he uses...

english: That Taliferro has a pretty impressive coiffe, doesn't he?
french: La coupe de Taliferro est impressionnante, pas vrai ?
russian: У этого Талиферро весьма впечатляющая укладка.
bulgarian: That Taliferro has a pretty impressive coiffe, doesn't he?

english: But there's no way he could deal with a regular working kitchen... he'd crack in a heartbeat!
french: Mais il ne tiendrait pas dans une vraie cuisine... Il craquerait en moins de deux !
russian: Но ему наверняка не управиться с настоящей рабочей кухней... Он бы сдулся за минуту!
bulgarian: But there's no way he could deal with a regular working kitchen... he'd crack in a heartbeat!

english: Taliferro talks big when he's running his $Cooking Challenge$...
french: Taliferro fait le malin quand il présente son $défi gastronomique$...
russian: Талиферро так важничает, когда проводит $смотр блюд$...
bulgarian: Taliferro talks big when he's running his $Cooking Challenge$...

english: His cooking skills are top-notch, but his personality? No, that's the kind of fella who needs a restaurant with his name on the sign.
french: Il cuisine comme personne, mais ce caractère... Non, c'est le genre de type à qui il faut un restaurant avec son nom sur la devanture.
russian: Готовит он на высшем уровне, но что за характер? Нет, этому парню нужна вывеска с его именем в ресторане.
bulgarian: His cooking skills are top-notch, but his personality? No, that's the kind of fella who needs a restaurant with his name on the sign.

english: You can't go hiring someone like Taliferro for your average kitchen.
french: Je n'irais pas engager un type comme Taliferro pour un restaurant normal.
russian: В обычную кулинарию нанимать Талиферро точно не стоит.
bulgarian: You can't go hiring someone like Taliferro for your average kitchen.

english: But one day she'll be the one giving out the recognition. Mark my words!
french: Un jour, c'est elle qui fera partie du jury. Tu peux me croire !
russian: Но настанет день, когда награды будет выдавать она. Запомни мои слова!
bulgarian: But one day she'll be the one giving out the recognition. Mark my words!

english: I'm proud of Reina for having her cooking recognized by a fancy chef like Taliferro...
french: Je suis fier qu'un chef de la trempe de Taliferro ait reconnu les talents de cuisinière de ma Reina...
russian: Я горжусь Рейной, что она получила признание такого модного шефа, как Талиферро...
bulgarian: I'm proud of Reina for having her cooking recognized by a fancy chef like Taliferro...

english: Maple's been going on about dyeing her hair pink. Kids ought to express themselves, but I don't know...
french: Maple n'arrête pas de dire qu'elle veut se teindre les cheveux en rose. Je sais que les enfants ont besoin de s'exprimer, mais quand même...
russian: Мэйпл всё хочет покрасить волосы в розовый. Понимаю, детям надо самовыражаться, но что-то я даже не знаю...
bulgarian: Maple's been going on about dyeing her hair pink. Kids ought to express themselves, but I don't know...

english: Vera and Josie are longtime friends, and they love an excuse to catch up. A haircut's as good a reason as any!
french: Vera et Jo sont des amies de longue date et elles cherchent toujours des occasions pour discuter. Un passage chez le coiffeur est parfait !
russian: Вера и Джози — давние подруги и всегда ищут повод поболтать. Ну а стрижка — чем не повод?
bulgarian: Vera and Josie are longtime friends, and they love an excuse to catch up. A haircut's as good a reason as any!

english: Josie said she's thinking about dyeing her hair purple... I bet she'd look great.
french: Jo dit qu'elle aimerait se teindre les cheveux en violet... Je suis sûr que ça lui irait bien.
russian: Джози говорит, подумывает покраситься в фиолетовый... думаю, ей пойдёт.
bulgarian: Josie said she's thinking about dyeing her hair purple... I bet she'd look great.

english: My hair was purple for a while, back when I toured with the band... might be fun to dye it again, take a little trip down memory lane.
french: J'avais les cheveux violets à l'époque où je tournais avec mon groupe... Ce serait marrant de les teindre à nouveau, en souvenir du bon vieux temps.
russian: У меня как-то были фиолетовые волосы, когда с группой ездил... может, покраситься снова, тряхнуть стариной?
bulgarian: My hair was purple for a while, back when I toured with the band... might be fun to dye it again, take a little trip down memory lane.

english: Last I heard, he had his business license revoked for selling the Royal Guard an expensive box of =White Wine=.
french: Si je me souviens bien, il avait perdu sa licence après avoir vendu très cher une caisse de =vin blanc= à la garde royale.
russian: Последнее, что я о нём слышал, — это что у него отобрали лицензию за продажу королевской страже дорогого ящика =белого вина=.
bulgarian: Last I heard, he had his business license revoked for selling the Royal Guard an expensive box of =White Wine=.

english: It was a fine vintage... if you like vinegar.
french: C'était un très bon cru... pour qui aime le vinaigre.
russian: Хорошей выдержки... если вы готовы пить уксус.
bulgarian: It was a fine vintage... if you like vinegar.

english: Surprised that Nora let Wheedle set up at the Saturday Market.
french: Je suis surpris que Nora ait donné un emplacement à Wheedle pour le marché du samedi.
russian: Удивительно, что Нора позволила Хлюсту открыть лавку на Субботнем базаре.
bulgarian: Surprised that Nora let Wheedle set up at the Saturday Market.

english: There was the time he opened a stall in the Capital that sold only tomatoes.
french: À une époque, il avait ouvert une échoppe à la capitale où il ne vendait que des tomates.
russian: Однажды он открыл в столице ларёк, где продавались только помидоры.
bulgarian: There was the time he opened a stall in the Capital that sold only tomatoes.

english: He called them Dragon Tomatoes, because these tomatoes were scaly like a dragon...
french: Mais des « tomates dragons », parce qu'elles avaient des écailles vertes comme celles d'un dragon...
russian: Он называл их «драконьи томаты», потому что у них была чешуя, как у дракона...
bulgarian: He called them Dragon Tomatoes, because these tomatoes were scaly like a dragon...

english: At least until the grand opening got rained on. All that green paint washed right into the gutter, along with Wheedle's credibility.
french: Manque de bol, il plut le jour de l'inauguration. Résultat, la peinture verte dont elles étaient recouvertes et la crédibilité de Wheedle finirent à l'égout.
russian: Пока на торжественном открытии не пошёл дождь. Вся зелёная краска с помидоров стекла в канаву, и туда же отправилась репутация Хлюста.
bulgarian: At least until the grand opening got rained on. All that green paint washed right into the gutter, along with Wheedle's credibility.

english: Whenever I see Wheedle, I always remember another one of his old business ventures...
french: Dès que je vois Wheedle, j'ai toujours en tête une de ses anciennes affaires.
russian: Когда я вижу Хлюста, я всегда вспоминаю одну из его старых коммерческих затей...
bulgarian: Whenever I see Wheedle, I always remember another one of his old business ventures...

english: I told myself I wouldn't buy anything from Wheedle, but I think Josie might like that $Snow Globe$...
french: Je me suis juré de ne jamais rien acheter à Wheedle, mais je crois que sa $boule à neige$ plaît à Jo...
russian: Я себе пообещал ничего не покупать у Хлюста, но, думаю, $снежный шар$ наверняка понравится Джози...
bulgarian: I told myself I wouldn't buy anything from Wheedle, but I think Josie might like that $Snow Globe$...

english: It's hard to forget a guy in a shiny three-piece suit going by the name 'Greedle.'
french: Ce n'est pas facile d'oublier un type en costard qui s'appelle « Oui, donne ».
russian: Парня по имени Хвост в сияющем костюме-тройке едва ли забудешь.
bulgarian: It's hard to forget a guy in a shiny three-piece suit going by the name 'Greedle.'

english: I feel like I met Wheedle a dozen times over while touring with the old band, but every time he was going by a different name.
french: J'ai l'impression d'avoir croisé Wheedle des dizaines de fois lors de mes tournées, mais il n'avait jamais le même nom.
russian: Кажется, я встречал Хлюста раз десять, когда мы путешествовали с группой. Но каждый раз у него было новое имя.
bulgarian: I feel like I met Wheedle a dozen times over while touring with the old band, but every time he was going by a different name.

english: Me and her Dad go way back. That man played the meanest saxophone you ever heard.
french: Son père et moi, on se connaît depuis longtemps. Il n'y avait pas meilleur joueur de saxophone.
russian:
Мы с её отцом познакомились много лет назад. Такого шустрого саксофониста ты ещё не

слышали

слышаласлышалслышало!
bulgarian: Me and her Dad go way back. That man played the meanest saxophone you ever heard.

english: Make sure you say hello to Zorel, [Ari]! She's an old family friend.
french: Surtout, va saluer Zorel, [Ari] ! C'est une vieille amie de la famille.
russian: Поздоровайся с Зорель, [Ari]! Она давно дружит с нашей семьёй.
bulgarian: Make sure you say hello to Zorel, [Ari]! She's an old family friend.

english: Between you and me though... I'd love to drink a beer out of it.
french: Entre nous... J'adorerais boire une bière dedans.
russian: Но между нами... Я бы с удовольствием выпил из него пива.
bulgarian: Between you and me though... I'd love to drink a beer out of it.

english: Errol tells me that $Ancient Crystal Goblet$ at the Museum is a very rare find, and probably was used in rituals.
french: Errol m'a dit que le $gobelet en cristal antique$ du musée était une découverte très rare et qu'il servait probablement lors de rituels.
russian: Эррол говорит, что $древний хрустальный бокал$ из музея использовался в ритуалах и что это — редчайшая находка.
bulgarian: Errol tells me that $Ancient Crystal Goblet$ at the Museum is a very rare find, and probably was used in rituals.

english: Just think of what kind of wine used to be in it!
french: Imagine un peu le type de vin qu'elle devait contenir autrefois !
russian: Только представь, какое там хранилось вино!
bulgarian: Just think of what kind of wine used to be in it!

english: That $Clay Amphora$ at the Museum is something else, huh?
french: Cette $amphore en argile$, au musée, c'est impressionnant, hein ?
russian: $Глиняная амфора$ в музее просто бесподобна.
bulgarian: That $Clay Amphora$ at the Museum is something else, huh?

english: I was over at the Museum and saw that $Mine Cricket$! I bet it plays a pretty little tune. The acoustics down there must be killer.
french: J'ai été au musée et j'ai vu le $criquet des mines$ ! Je parie qu'il produit un son très musical. L'acoustique là en bas doit être exceptionnelle.
russian: Я был в музее и увидел того $шахтенного сверчка$! Бьюсь об заклад, он играет милую мелодию. Акустика там внизу, должно быть, шикарная.
bulgarian: I was over at the Museum and saw that $Mine Cricket$! I bet it plays a pretty little tune. The acoustics down there must be killer.

english: It might be fun to lug my lute out there and play a little duet.
french: Ça pourrait être drôle que j'arrive avec mon luth pour faire un petit duo.
russian: Может, мне притащить туда свою лютню и сыграть с ней дуэт?
bulgarian: It might be fun to lug my lute out there and play a little duet.

english: That $Mist Flute$ that got added to the Museum's collection... it lets out a little tune every so often.
french: La $flûte de brume$ qui a été ajoutée aux collections du musée... Elle émet de temps à autre une petite mélodie.
russian: В музейной коллекции недавно появилась $туманная флейта$... И она время от времени издаёт звуки.
bulgarian: That $Mist Flute$ that got added to the Museum's collection... it lets out a little tune every so often.

english: But as a bartender, that just doesn't sound right to me!
french: En tant que gérant d'une taverne, je trouve que quelque chose cloche !
russian: Но как бармен я с этим не могу согласиться!
bulgarian: But as a bartender, that just doesn't sound right to me!

english: Eiland thinks the $Ritual Chalice$ at the Museum probably only held water...
french: Eiland pense que le $calice rituel$, au musée, ne contenait sans doute que de l'eau...
russian: Эйланд думает, что $ритуальный кубок$ в музее, скорее всего, использовали только для воды...
bulgarian: Eiland thinks the $Ritual Chalice$ at the Museum probably only held water...

english: We were so disappointed when Errol said it was empty!
french: On a été très déçus quand Errol nous a dit qu'elle était vide !
russian: Так разочаровались, когда Эррол сказал, что она пустая!
bulgarian: We were so disappointed when Errol said it was empty!

english: Holt and I saw that $Tin Lunchbox$ at the Museum and started making bets on who would eat whatever was inside.
french: Holt et moi, on a vu la $gamelle en étain$ au musée et on a commencé à parier pour savoir qui mangerait son contenu.
russian: Мы с Хольтом увидели $кастрюлю$ в музее и начали спорить, кто бы съел её содержимое.
bulgarian: Holt and I saw that $Tin Lunchbox$ at the Museum and started making bets on who would eat whatever was inside.
